turns.content: Treat molecular vibration as a quantum harmonic oscillator with E_n=(n+1/2)hc times the vibrational wavenumber. At temperature T, define T=hc times the wavenumber divided by kT and derive the normalized Boltzmann population P_n, noting how the zero-point term cancels.

For I2 with vibrational wavenumber 208 cm^-1 at 298 K, evaluate x using k=6.626e-34 J s, c=3.00e10 cm s^-1, and k=1.38e-23 J K^-1. Then evaluate the geometric vibrational partition factor 1/(1-exp(-x)).
Specialize the normalized population formula to n=2 and leave it in terms of x or exponentials before numerical evaluation.
Evaluate the n=2 population numerically using the stated precision of the constants.
Check the result by viewing the normalized populations as a geometric distribution: verify their common ratio and that summing all levels gives one.
Distinguish the raw Boltzmann weight exp(-2x) from the probability P_2. Why must the raw weight be divided by the partition sum?
Use the normalization check to assess whether setting the partition sum equal to one would be justified at this temperature and spacing.
Report the probability that I2 occupies n=2 at 298 K and state the normalization used.
